privacy_policy_section1_content: Nilu collects health data necessary for period tracking. This includes cycle dates, symptoms, mood logs, and physical signs. Your data is primarily stored on your device. If you use pregnancy mode, this also includes your pregnancy record (last period and due date; how the pregnancy ended — saying so is optional), your appointments and notes, whether you are trying to conceive, and the blood pressure and weight readings you enter. These records are stored encrypted on your device and never leave it unless you export them.
privacy_policy_section2_content: Your data is used to provide cycle predictions, health suggestions and the partner features. Your health data is not used for ad targeting and is not sent to ad networks. The services we rely on to run the app (section 5) receive only what their own function requires.
privacy_policy_section3_content: When you use the partner feature, your partner receives only the intimacy status you send (desire and affection needs). Your cycle dates, symptoms, pain records and notes are not sent to your partner — they stay on your device. You can turn sharing off completely at any time. Your pregnancy and postnatal records are not sent to your partner either.
privacy_policy_section4_content: Health data on your device is stored encrypted. Data you send to your partner is encrypted in transit and stored encrypted on the server. This is not end-to-end encryption: because the keys are held by the service provider, the provider can technically access that data. Data that never leaves your device is unaffected.
privacy_policy_section5_content: The app uses: Firebase (Google) for account creation, partner pairing and the notification token; Sign in with Apple for authentication; RevenueCat and Apple for subscription verification; Google AdMob for ads in the free version. Each service receives only the data its own function requires. Your cycle records, symptoms, pain records and notes are not sent to any of them. These services may store data on servers outside your country. Your pregnancy and postnatal records and your blood pressure and weight readings are not sent to these services either.
privacy_policy_section6_content: The free version shows banner ads. Ads are not personalised: the app sends no health data, cycle information or profile data to the ad network. To serve an ad, the network receives technical information about your device and connection (such as your IP address). Premium removes ads.
privacy_policy_section7_content: The camera is used only to scan a partner QR code; no image is stored or sent anywhere. Face ID or your device passcode is used only for the app lock, and verification happens on your device. If you allow notifications, reminders are prepared on your device and their contents are not sent anywhere. If you allow Apple Health access, the app reads your menstrual flow, sleep and resting heart rate, and writes the period days you record back to Apple Health. You can withdraw any of these permissions at any time in iOS settings. If you turn on discreet notifications, the lock screen does not show what a reminder is about.
privacy_policy_section8_content: Your health records stay on your device until you delete them. Server-side data — intimacy status, pairing code and the account record — remains until you delete your account or disconnect from your partner. Deleting your account removes all of it: the pairing code is revoked, intimacy records and the account are deleted, and on-device data is wiped. This cannot be undone.
privacy_policy_section9_content: You can export, edit, restore from a backup or completely delete your data at any time. To exercise your rights of access, rectification, erasure, portability and objection, contact us at [EMAIL ADDRESS]. Data controller: Hürkan Çelebi, Bağcılar/İstanbul, Türkiye.
privacy_policy_section10_content: When this policy changes, the “last updated” date above is revised. You can always read the current text inside the app.
terms_section1_content: By downloading and using the Nilu app, you agree to these terms of service. If you do not agree to these terms, please do not use the app.
terms_section2_content: Nilu is a health app for period tracking and partner notification. The app does not provide medical diagnosis and is not a substitute for professional health care. Always consult a healthcare professional for medical decisions. This also applies to pregnancy and postnatal tracking: these sections do not replace care from your doctor, midwife or health service; warning signs and blood pressure alerts are not a diagnosis, they only point you to care. In an emergency, call your local emergency number.
terms_section3_content: This app is intended for people aged 12 and over. If you are not of legal age where you live, use the app only with the permission of a parent or guardian. If you create an account, you confirm that the information you provide is accurate.
terms_section4_content: The core features are free: cycle tracking, logging, the calendar, reminders and creating a restorable backup. The free version shows banner ads; ads are not personalised and no health data is sent to the ad network (see the Privacy Policy). A Premium subscription removes ads and unlocks: your full cycle history, symptom–phase analysis, the summary and table files you can take to a clinician, and custom themes. Pregnancy and postnatal tracking is free too: appointments and their reminders, warning signs, measurement alerts and the on-screen appointment summary. Sharing the appointment summary as a file is part of Premium.
terms_section5_content: Premium features are available via subscription. Subscriptions automatically renew. Cancellation must be made at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. You can manage your subscription in your App Store settings.
terms_section6_content: Your health records are stored on your device. If you delete the app, lose your device or reset it, those records cannot be recovered. Exporting and keeping a copy of your data is your responsibility; creating a backup is free. Restoring a backup does not delete anything on your device — only missing entries are added.
terms_section7_content: Use the app to track your own health data. Do not set up partner pairing without the other person's knowledge and consent: whoever you give your pairing code to will see the data you choose to share. Reverse engineering the app, using it with automated tools, or attempting to access other people's data is prohibited.
terms_section8_content: The texts, health library content, exercises, images and software in the app belong to us and are protected by copyright. They may not be copied, distributed or used to create derivative works beyond personal use. Your own records belong to you.
terms_section9_content: You can delete your account from inside the app at any time; this cannot be undone. We may end your access if these terms are breached. Deleting your account does not automatically cancel an active subscription — you must cancel it separately in App Store settings.
terms_section10_content: The app is provided 'as is'. Cycle predictions are based on statistical models and 100% accuracy is not guaranteed. Do not rely solely on this app for birth control or pregnancy planning. Gestational age and due date calculations are estimates too; the date your doctor gives you takes priority.
terms_section11_content: When these terms change, the “last updated” date above is revised. You can always read the current text inside the app. Continuing to use the app after a change means you accept the new terms.
terms_section12_content: These terms are governed by the laws of Türkiye; the courts and enforcement offices of Istanbul shall have jurisdiction over disputes. For questions, contact us at [EMAIL ADDRESS].

article_hormones_intro: Hormone levels shift continuously across your cycle. Those shifts affect more than bleeding — they touch your energy, your sleep and your mood. Knowing what happens in each phase makes the ups and downs easier to make sense of.
article_hormones_b1: A cycle runs from the first day of one period to the first day of the next. For most people it is around 28 days, but anywhere from 21 to 35 days is commonly considered typical. Sources draw the line slightly differently; this app uses the 24–38 day range described in the section below. Bleeding usually lasts 2 to 7 days, about 5 on average, and tends to be heaviest on the first two days.
article_hormones_b2: When estrogen and progesterone drop to their lowest, the uterine lining sheds — that is your period. As bleeding ends, estrogen starts climbing again and the lining rebuilds. Energy and focus often pick up during this stretch.
article_hormones_b3: LH, released by your brain, tells the ovary to release an egg. It surges about 36 hours before ovulation and peaks around 12 hours before. Ovulation usually falls 12 to 16 days before your next period starts. Because sperm can survive up to 7 days, the fertile window is wider than ovulation day alone.
article_hormones_h4: Luteal phase and when to see a doctor
article_hormones_b4:
After ovulation, progesterone rises and prepares the lining for a possible pregnancy. If there is no pregnancy, hormones fall again and the cycle restarts.

It is worth seeing a clinician if your cycle is regularly shorter than 24 days or longer than 38, if it changes suddenly, or if your bleeding is very heavy.
article_pms_intro: Premenstrual symptoms are common: more than 90% of women report some. They usually appear in the five days before a period and ease within four days after bleeding starts.
article_pms_b1: The evidence clusters around a few nutrients. Calcium may reduce fatigue, cravings and low mood. Vitamin B6 may help with moodiness, irritability, bloating and anxiety. Magnesium may ease migraine-type headaches. Polyunsaturated fatty acids (1–2 grams a day) may reduce cramps and other symptoms.
article_pms_b2: Regular aerobic exercise throughout the month, about eight hours of sleep a night, and stress-lowering practices such as yoga, massage or meditation are all recommended. Cutting back on caffeine, salt and sugar in the two weeks before your period is another suggested step. Smaller, more frequent meals help some people.
article_pms_b3: See a clinician if lifestyle changes have not helped or your symptoms are affecting daily life. It is also worth asking before starting supplements: this page is general information, not personal medical advice.
article_partner_intro: Talking to your partner about your cycle is not complaining — it is sharing the map of something you both live with. When they know what to expect, there is less misreading, and less of a burden on you to explain it from scratch every time.
article_partner_b1: Premenstrual symptoms typically start in the five days before bleeding and ease within four days after it begins. Sharing that shows a mood shift is a known pattern, not a personal stance. Partner sharing in the app can be a way into that conversation: the intimacy status you choose to send reaches them. Your cycle data never leaves your device, so what you tell them is still your call.
article_partner_b2: "Be understanding" stays abstract. "Let us not make evening plans this week", "could you bring me a hot water bottle", "I want to be alone today and I am not angry with you" — concrete sentences let the other person know what to actually do.
article_partner_b3: A conversation opened at peak symptoms turns into an argument easily. Talking on a comfortable day in your cycle makes it easier for both of you to listen without getting defensive. Noting together what worked saves you from having the same conversation next cycle.
article_mood_intro: Mood changes before a period are common and real. Health services say the cause is not fully understood, and that it is likely tied to shifting hormone levels across the cycle — with some people affected more than others.
article_mood_b1: Mood swings, feeling low or irritable, anxiety and tearfulness are frequently reported. They can come alongside tiredness, trouble sleeping, bloating, breast tenderness, headaches and appetite changes.
article_mood_b2:
Regular exercise, a balanced diet, enough sleep and stress-lowering practices like yoga or meditation are recommended. Avoiding smoking and heavy drinking is on the list too.

Logging your symptoms across a few cycles pays off: seeing the pattern helps you plan, and gives you something concrete to show a clinician.
article_mood_b3:
See a clinician if symptoms are affecting your daily life or lifestyle changes are not enough. Premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) is a separate, more severe condition that can bring intense anxiety, anger or depression.

If you are having thoughts of harming yourself or of suicide, do not carry that alone — reach emergency services or someone close to you without delay.
article_iron_intro: Heavy periods are one of the most common causes of iron deficiency anaemia. Without enough iron, your blood cannot carry oxygen well, and that usually shows up first as tiredness.
article_iron_b1: The most common are tiredness, shortness of breath, heart palpitations, pale skin and headaches. Less commonly: ringing in the ears, a changed sense of taste, mouth ulcers, a sore tongue, hair loss, spoon-shaped nails and restless legs syndrome.
article_iron_b2:
Iron-rich foods include dark-green leafy vegetables such as watercress and curly kale, fortified cereals and bread, meat, dried fruit such as apricots, prunes and raisins, and beans, peas and lentils.

Iron from plants absorbs better alongside vitamin C, so adding orange, peppers or tomato to a meal helps. Tea, coffee, dairy and foods high in phytic acid make iron harder to absorb, so they are best kept away from the meal itself.
article_iron_b3: If you have these signs, see a clinician: iron deficiency shows up on a simple blood test, and it is worth checking whether something other than bleeding is behind it. Do not start iron supplements without medical advice — iron you do not need can be harmful.
article_disclaimer: This is general information, not personal medical advice. If something worries you, speak to a health professional.

cycle_settings_contraception_desc: Pill, hormonal IUD, implant or injection. When on, ovulation and fertility estimates are hidden — these methods usually suppress ovulation.
bleeding_check_intro: What counts as "heavy" varies a lot between people. Below are the concrete signs the NHS lists — tick the ones that apply to you.
bleeding_sign_frequent_changes: I change my pad or tampon every 1–2 hours
bleeding_sign_double_protection: I use more than one product at once (e.g. pad and tampon)
bleeding_sign_longer_than_seven: My bleeding lasts longer than 7 days
bleeding_sign_large_clots: I pass clots larger than about 2.5 cm
bleeding_sign_flooding: It bleeds through onto my clothes or bedding
bleeding_sign_limits_life: I skip activities or miss work because of the bleeding
bleeding_sign_tiredness: It comes with tiredness or shortness of breath
bleeding_check_result_body: What you ticked fits the description of heavy bleeding. That is not a diagnosis on its own, but it is worth having looked at — heavy bleeding has many treatable causes.
bleeding_check_iron_title: Ask about your iron levels too
bleeding_check_iron_body: Heavy bleeding with tiredness alongside it. Heavy periods are one of the most common causes of iron deficiency anaemia, and a simple blood test shows it.
bleeding_check_none_body: Tick anything that applies to you. If none of it does, your bleeding is most likely in the usual range.
alert_short_title: Your cycles are consistently shorter than 24 days
alert_short_body: Every cycle in your records is under 24 days. There are many possible reasons; it is worth asking a clinician.
alert_long_title: Your cycles are consistently longer than 38 days
alert_long_body: Every cycle in your records is over 38 days. Infrequent or irregular periods are worth having looked at.
alert_variable_body: There are more than 8 days between your shortest and longest cycle. Stress, sleep and travel explain some variation; a sudden change is worth asking about.
alert_spotting_body: You've logged bleeding outside your periods {count} times. It can happen around ovulation or while adjusting to a new contraceptive. If it keeps happening, it's worth mentioning to a clinician.
alert_disclaimer: This is not a diagnosis. The app only looks at the dates you logged.
day_detail_pain_limited: The pain stopped me doing normal activities today
log_pain_when_hint: These are details clinicians ask about specifically. Logging them can speed up a diagnosis.
partner_qr_gen_rotate_hint: Refreshing stops any QR code you shared earlier from working.
partner_scan_error_unknown: This code is no longer valid. Ask your partner for a new one.
partner_scan_requested: Request sent. You will see their cycle once they approve.
partner_requests_hint: Nobody sees your cycle until you approve. Reject anything you did not expect.
partner_request_approved: Approved. Your partner can now see what you share.
home_period_early_body: Your period was expected in {n} days, on {date}. If we record it as starting today, the predictions will be recalculated.
home_period_toggle_failed: This day could not be marked.
privacy_ads_notice: The free version shows ads. They are not personalised: your health data is never used for advertising and you are not targeted. Premium has no ads.
premium_feature_noads_desc: Removes the banner ads shown in the free version.
care_tr_screen_combined_title: Nuchal translucency scan and combined test
care_condition_no_combined: If the combined test wasn't done
care_condition_rh_negative: If you are Rh-negative and your partner is Rh-positive
care_condition_tetanus_history: If needed based on your vaccination history
care_condition_no_anemia: If you don't have anaemia — if you do, your doctor sets the dose
notif_care_window_body: It's time for this check-up. If you haven't booked it yet, now is a good moment.
notif_discreet_body: You have a reminder for today.
notif_folic_acid_body: If you're planning a pregnancy, starting folic acid at least 1 month beforehand is recommended. Ask your doctor about the dose.
notif_consult_body: You've been trying to conceive for a while. An evaluation is recommended at this point — it doesn't mean something is wrong.
danger_intro: If you notice any of the following, seek care right away.
danger_call_local: In an emergency, call your local emergency number.
danger_preg_movements: Baby moving less, or a change in movements
danger_preg_swelling: Swelling of the face, hands or legs
danger_preg_daily_activities: Being unable to manage your daily activities
danger_pp_bleeding: Vaginal bleeding: soaking more than 2–3 pads in 20–30 minutes, clots or bright red bleeding; bleeding that increases again after easing, or keeps getting heavier
danger_pp_breathing: Shortness of breath, chest pain, fast breathing, coughing or a racing heart — sometimes with leg pain
danger_pp_urination: Pain when passing urine, or leaking urine
danger_movements_note_body: There's no need to count movements. Get to know your baby's own pattern; if movements slow down or change, get checked the same day — don't wait until tomorrow.
danger_pp_mental_body: Thoughts of harming yourself or your baby, seeing or hearing things that aren't there, or sudden extreme changes in mood are an emergency. Get help straight away.
calendar_preg_bleeding_note: In pregnancy, bleeding isn't recorded as a period. If you have any bleeding, even a little, contact your doctor or midwife.
calendar_pp_bleeding_note: After birth, bleeding (lochia) isn't recorded as a period; you can log how it's going each day from the home screen.
care_empty: No appointments yet. You can add the check-ups your doctor or midwife gives you; we'll remind you the evening before.
care_source_antenatal: This schedule follows the Turkish Ministry of Health antenatal care guideline (2018). The schedule your doctor recommends comes first.
care_source_postnatal: This schedule follows the Turkish Ministry of Health postnatal care guideline (2018). The schedule your doctor or midwife recommends comes first.
notif_discreet_setting_body: On the lock screen, notifications only say "You have a reminder for today" instead of the details.
pp_concern_body: Bleeding that gets heavier instead of lighter is one of the signs that need urgent care. Contact a health service now.
pp_concern_reincrease_title: Your bleeding has increased again after easing
preg_danger_entry_body: Signs that need care right away
pp_info_fertility: You can get pregnant before your first period: ovulation happens before it. Ask your doctor about contraception.
pp_info_supplements: According to the guideline, iron and vitamin D supplements continue after birth.
pp_lochia_body: Bleeding after birth (lochia) usually gets lighter over time. Log it each day and we'll watch the trend — and tell you if it gets heavier again.
preg_bleeding_dialog_body: In pregnancy, bleeding — even a little — is a sign to contact your doctor, midwife or a health service. Your entry has been saved.
preg_due_source_body: Did the date {date} come from your doctor? A date from your doctor takes priority over the app's estimate.
preg_end_intro: You're ending pregnancy tracking. You don't have to say what happened.
preg_end_what_happens: Your pregnancy record and appointments aren't deleted — they stay in your history. Pregnancy reminders stop right away.
preg_setup_care_own_body: You add the appointments your doctor or midwife gives you.
preg_setup_care_tr_body: 4 antenatal visits, screenings and supplements. You can edit every item.
preg_setup_change_bleeding: Bleeding won't be recorded as a period: in pregnancy, bleeding is a sign to check with your doctor.
preg_setup_change_predictions: Period and fertility predictions will pause.
preg_setup_change_reminders: Reminders will follow your pregnancy check-ups.
preg_setup_due_method_clinician: Based on the date from your doctor.
preg_setup_due_method_lmp: Calculated from your last period and your {n}-day cycle. If your doctor gives you a different date, enter that — it takes priority.
preg_setup_due_passed: With this date, the due date would already have passed. Please check the date.
preg_setup_pick_lmp: Choose the first day of your last period
preg_week_day_sentence_one: You are {w} weeks and 1 day pregnant
preg_week_day_sentence: You are {w} weeks and {d} days pregnant
profile_preg_ttc_body: Reminds you about folic acid and when to see a doctor.
log_preg_symptom_note: In pregnancy, a severe headache, sudden swelling of the face, hands or legs, vomiting that won't stop, or unexplained itching are signs to contact your doctor or midwife without waiting.
log_measure_hint: Optional. Measure your blood pressure sitting down after resting for a few minutes, with your arm at heart level.
log_measure_invalid: One of the measurements isn't valid. Enter weight in kg and blood pressure with both numbers (e.g. 120 / 80).
bp_high_body: {s}/{d} mmHg. In pregnancy and after birth, 140/90 or higher should be reported to your doctor or midwife. Rest sitting down for a few minutes and measure again; if it's still high, contact them the same day. If you also have a headache, vision problems or sudden swelling, get care without waiting.
bp_severe_title: Your blood pressure is very high
bp_severe_body: {s}/{d} mmHg. 160/110 or higher needs urgent assessment. Get care now — don't wait.
care_summary_intro: To show your doctor or midwife at your appointment. It is made only from what you have logged and does not diagnose anything.
reminder_permission_body_care: To remind you of your check-ups, screenings and appointments in time, we need notification permission. Notifications are prepared on your device; their content is never sent anywhere.
bp_symptoms_body: {s}/{d} mmHg together with a headache, swelling or vomiting can be a sign of pre-eclampsia. In pregnancy and after birth this needs to be checked without waiting. Contact a health service now.
pp_return_subtitle: Ends postnatal tracking; nothing is deleted
pp_return_body: You're returning to period tracking. Your birth record, appointments and notes are kept; postnatal reminders stop. When your first period comes, you can mark it in the calendar or on the home screen. Predictions restart once your first cycle is complete.
